definitions.gloss: family-friendly boss; manager who supports staff work-life balance
definitions.explanation: A manager who actively backs subordinates' childcare and family life — approving leave, cutting overtime, adjusting workloads — while still delivering results. A coined term promoted in workplace-reform campaigns since the mid-2010s.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はイクボスとして{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: She is well known as a family-friendly manager.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}はイクボスの{育成|いくせい}に{力|ちから}を{入|い}れている。
examples.english: The company is putting effort into developing family-friendly managers.

examples.japanese: {部下|ぶか}の{育児休業|いくじきゅうぎょう}を{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}のこととして{認|みと}める{上司|じょうし}が、いわゆるイクボスだ。
examples.english: A boss who treats a subordinate's parental leave as a matter of course is what is called an ikubosu.

notes:
Coined from {育|いく} (of {育児|いくじ}, childcare) + English "boss", on the model of イクメン (a father actively involved in childcare). Companies and local governments run イクボス{宣言|せんげん} campaigns in which managers publicly commit to the role.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- イクボス{宣言|せんげん}: a public pledge to be a family-friendly manager
- イクボス{研修|けんしゅう}: training for family-friendly managers
- イクボスを{目指|めざ}す: to aim to be a family-friendly manager

SIMILAR WORDS:
- イクメン: a hands-on father — about a man's own parenting, not his management of others
- {働|はたら}き{方|かた}{改革|かいかく}: workplace reform — the wider policy movement the term belongs to
